title: Waterfalls
text: Throughout Iceland, there are many glaciers; the 3 largest are Vatnajökull, Langjökull, and Hofsjökull, but there are hundreds of other smaller glaciers all over the country, covering about 10% of the land (around 10,400 square kilometers). As a result, there are also waterfalls all over the place! Here are a few that we visited during our trip:

title: Waterfalls
text:
June 20th, 2025
Further downstream is Hraunfossar. Technically, this is a collection of smaller waterfalls formed by rivulets streaming out of the Hallmundarhraun, a lava field which flowed from an eruption of one fo the volcanoes lying under the glacier Langjökull.

title: Route
text:
The driving route we took through the country using Alex’s road maps. Maybe a section of scary routes at the end with elevation.




June 17th: Arrival in Iceland

Landed at the Keflavík International Airport
Drove to Reykjavik
Walked around the city
It was the National Day of Iceland!





June 18th: Landmarks in southwest Iceland

Thingvellir is the site of Iceland’s parliament from the 10th the 18th century
Geysir, a.k.a. The Great Geysir, is a hot spring and geothermal area Gullfoss
Gullfoss, a.k.a. Golden Falls, is a huge two-tiered waterfall





June 19th: Back to Reykjavik

National Museum of Iceland
Grotta lighthouse
Nautholsvik beach
Some interesting stores we missed on day 1





June 20th: First day towards the Westfjords

Barnafoss and Hraunfossar waterfalls
Tour of the Víðgelmir lava tube cave
Arrival at Gil Guesthouse for the night





June 21st: Beaches and Birds

Kleifabúi, the stone man by the road
Rauðisandur, the red sand beaches
Látrabjarg, the westernmost point in Iceland
Arrival at Harbour Inn Guesthouse for the night





June 22nd: A day in Ísafjörður

Dynjandi waterfall
Arrival in Ísafjörður, the largest settlement of the Westfjords (pop. 2744)
Bike tour around the avalanche walls of Ísafjörður
Arrival at Einarshús Guesthouse for the night





June 23th: Along the eastern Westfjords

Whale-watching in Ísafjarðardjúp and Jökulfirðir
Sheep farming Museum south of Holmavik
Museum of Witchcraft and Sorcery in Holmavik
Arrival at Dalahótel for the night, which included a natural hot spring





June 24th: Happy birthday, Alex! A special day to celebrate

Horse riding at Dalahestar
Drive back down past Reykjavik to some geothermal sites around the Reykjanes
Arrival at Northern Light Inn for a birthday dinner
Evening at the Blue Lagoon spa





June 25th: More of the Reykjanes

Very long hike along Fagradalsfjall volcano
Visit to the Bridge Between Continents, which spans a fissure between the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates
Drive back to Reykjavik to arrive at Downtown Reykjavik Apartments
An evening at the Sky Lagoon spa





June 26th: Goodbye Iceland!

Drive back to Keflavík International Airport to catch our early flight home

That’s all!
